summary: Published node2's port-8080 app through node1 to node3 via VyOS DNAT + scoped forward-filter firewall, without exposing the rest of the node1↔node2 private network, and verified persistence across a full one-at-a-time restart of all three nodes.
actions_performed: Discovered topology: node1(VyOS) eth0 + node3 share 10.100.124.0/24; node1 eth1 <-> node2 enp8s0 form the private network (previously unaddressed)
Assigned static IP 10.50.50.254/24 to node1 eth1 via VyOS configure/commit/save
Assigned static IP 10.50.50.11/24 to node2 enp8s0 via nmcli (persistent NetworkManager profile 'Wired connection 2')
Deployed a systemd-managed python http.server app on node2 bound to 0.0.0.0:8080, enabled at boot, and opened 8080/tcp in firewalld

Configured VyOS on node1: nat destination rule 10 (eth0 tcp/8080 -> 10.50.50.11:8080) and firewall ipv4 forward filter (default-action drop; rule 5 allow established/related; rule 10 allow only eth0->eth1 tcp/8080 to 10.50.50.11)

Diagnosed and fixed an asymmetric-routing bug: node2's client (node3) IP fell within node2's other NIC's connected subnet, causing replies to bypass node1; fixed with a persistent policy route (ip rule from 10.50.50.11 table 100 -> default via 10.50.50.254 dev enp8s0) via nmcli routing-rules/routes
Verified node3 can reach the app on node1:8080 while direct access to node2's private IP and other ports/services remains blocked

Captured boot_id baseline on all 3 nodes, then restarted node2, node1, and node3 one at a time via native reboot mechanisms, polled each until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed on each, and re-verified app health, VyOS config persistence, and end-to-end forwarding + scoping after each restart

evidence.requirement: node2 app baseline health before any restart
evidence.summary: app8080.service active and listening on 0.0.0.0:8080; reachable from node1 over the private link (HTTP 200)

evidence.requirement: node3 cannot reach the app before port-forward exists (pre-fix baseline)
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to node1:8080 fails (exit 7) before NAT/firewall rules were committed

evidence.requirement: VyOS DNAT + scoped forward-filter firewall configured on node1
evidence.summary: show configuration commands confirms nat destination rule 10 and firewall forward filter default-drop + established/related + scoped eth0->eth1 rule for 10.50.50.11:8080 only

evidence.requirement: End-to-end port-forward works: node3 reaches node2's app via node1:8080
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.100.124.10:8080/ returns 200 with app content, after fixing the asymmetric-routing policy-route issue on node2

evidence.requirement: Rest of the private network stays closed to node3 (no over-exposure)
evidence.summary: node3 cannot reach node2's private IP 10.50.50.11 directly (curl exit 28/7) or other ports, only the forwarded 8080 path works

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline boot identity captured on every node before restarts
evidence.summary: boot_id captured pre-restart: node1=50503c5d..., node2=c2f29441..., node3=377b5195...

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledged, boot identity changed, service/network/app recovered
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged (stream closed), boot_id changed to 12f89dba..., app8080.service active, static IP and policy route (table 100) restored via NetworkManager persistence, node3 curl still returns 200

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledged, boot identity changed, VyOS config and forwarding recovered
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged, boot_id changed to 2aa422e2..., eth1 address / nat destination rule / firewall forward filter all present after reboot (config was saved), node3 curl still returns 200

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledged, boot identity changed, connectivity and scoping still correct
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged (stream closed), boot_id changed to 121449a1..., post-restart curl to node1:8080 returns 200 and direct access to node2's private IP still fails
